mcqs.question: Which of the following compound inequalities has the solution set \((-\infty,2) \cup (5,\infty)\)?
mcqs.explanation: The inequality "x < 2 or x > 5" represents all real numbers less than 2 together with all numbers greater than 5, which is exactly the interval \((-\infty,2) \cup (5,\infty)\). Option B gives a conjunction, producing no numbers; Option C gives a single interval (2,5); Option D includes the endpoints, giving \((-\infty,2] \cup [5,\infty)\).

mcqs.question: The solution set of a certain linear inequality in one variable is \((-4,1] \cup [3,\infty)\). Which of the following statements is always true for any real number x satisfying the inequality?
mcqs.explanation: The given set consists of two parts: numbers strictly greater than -4 but at most 1, and numbers greater than or equal to 3. Option B states exactly that. Option A incorrectly includes x \le -4, which is not in the set. Option C changes the inequality signs at the endpoints. Option D describes a completely different region.

mcqs.question: Solve the inequality: 5 - 2x > 9. Which of the following describes the solution set?
mcqs.explanation: Starting with 5 - 2x > 9, subtract 5 to get -2x > 4. Dividing by -2 (and reversing the inequality sign) yields x < -2. Hence option B is correct. The other options either reverse the inequality or give unrelated bounds.

mcqs.learning_point: Represent solutions on a number line
mcqs.question: Which number‑line diagram correctly represents the solution of the inequality x \ge 3?

options.A: A closed circle at 3 with a solid arrow extending to the right.
options.B: An open circle at 3 with a solid arrow extending to the right.
options.C: A closed circle at 3 with a solid arrow extending to the left.
options.D: An open circle at 3 with a solid arrow extending to the left.

mcqs.answer: A closed circle at 3 with a solid arrow extending to the right.
mcqs.explanation: The inequality x \ge 3 includes the endpoint 3, so the point 3 is shown as a closed (filled) circle. Since all numbers greater than 3 also satisfy the inequality, the arrow points to the right. Options B, C, and D either use an open circle (excluding 3) or point in the wrong direction.

mcqs.question: Which interval notation correctly represents the solution set of the compound inequality x > -1 and x \le 4?
mcqs.explanation: The condition x > -1 excludes -1, giving an open parenthesis on the left, while x \le 4 includes 4, giving a closed bracket on the right. Hence the correct interval is (-1,4]. Options B and D incorrectly include -1, and option C represents a completely different set.

mcqs.question: A student must score at least 40 marks but not more than 70 marks in a test. Which inequality correctly represents the possible scores (x) of the student?
mcqs.explanation: ‘At least 40’ means x is greater than or equal to 40, and ‘not more than 70’ means x is less than or equal to 70. Both conditions together give 40 \le x \le 70. Option A excludes the endpoints, option C is equivalent to A, and option D uses ‘or’, which would allow scores outside the required range.

mcqs.question: The solution set of the inequality 2x - 5 \le 9 is \(( -\infty,7]\). Which statement correctly interprets this solution set?

options.A: All real numbers less than or equal to 7 satisfy the inequality.
options.B: All real numbers greater than 7 satisfy the inequality.
options.C: Only the number 7 satisfies the inequality.
options.D: No real number satisfies the inequality.

mcqs.answer: All real numbers less than or equal to 7 satisfy the inequality.
mcqs.explanation: The interval \(( -\infty,7]\) includes every real number up to and including 7. Therefore every x \le 7 makes 2x - 5 \le 9 true. Options B, C, and D contradict the interval description.

mcqs.question: A rectangular garden has length L meters and a fixed width of 5 m. The condition that the perimeter exceeds 50 m leads to the inequality 2L + 2(5) > 50. Which of the following gives the correct solution for L?
mcqs.explanation: Simplify the inequality: 2L + 10 > 50 \Rightarrow 2L > 40 \Rightarrow L > 20. Wait, correction: 2L + 10 > 50 gives 2L > 40, so L > 20. However the original perimeter condition should be 2(L + 5) > 50, which simplifies to L + 5 > 25, giving L > 20. The provided inequality 2L + 2(5) > 50 is equivalent to 2L + 10 > 50, leading to L > 20. Therefore the correct answer is L > 20, which corresponds to option A. (Corrected answer: option A).
